rule: A local tax is applied only when the user selects that jurisdiction. New York City tax is never applied to the rest of New York. A custom percent overrides the selected jurisdiction and is applied to gross wages. Local rates change; if a named place’s rate differs from our lastVerified date, use the custom local rate field.

jurisdictions.name: New York City
jurisdictions.residentOnlyNote: New York City income tax applies to residents of the five boroughs. Working in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, or Staten Island does not, by itself, create a city income tax.

source.name: New York State, New York City tax rates

jurisdictions.notes: Resident rates of 3.078%, 3.762%, 3.819%, and 3.876% have been the NYC schedule for years and remain the rates published for recent IT-201 instructions. The base here is New York taxable income (wages after the New York standard deduction and deductions that reduce New York wages). NYC modifications, the household credit, and the school tax credit are not modeled, so a real return can differ by a few hundred dollars.

jurisdictions.name: Yonkers
jurisdictions.sourceLabel: Yonkers resident surcharge / nonresident earnings tax

source.name: New York State, Yonkers tax

jurisdictions.notes: Yonkers residents pay a surcharge of 16.75% of their net New York State tax. Nonresidents who work in Yonkers pay a 0.50% earnings tax on wages sourced to the city. The resident surcharge is not a flat wage percent, so it moves when state tax moves.

jurisdictions.name: Philadelphia

source.name: City of Philadelphia Department of Revenue, wage tax cut effective July 1, 2025

jurisdictions.notes: Effective July 1, 2025 (fiscal year 2026), the wage and earnings tax is 3.74% for residents and 3.43% for nonresidents. Residents owe it on wages wherever earned. Nonresidents owe it on wages earned in the city. Traditional 401(k) deferrals and most cafeteria-plan amounts stay in the wage-tax base in this model. The city has scheduled further small reductions through FY2030; those future rates are not used here.

jurisdictions.name: Pittsburgh

source.name: City of Pittsburgh, Earned Income Tax

jurisdictions.notes: City of Pittsburgh publishes a 3% resident earned income tax (1% city + 2% Pittsburgh Public Schools) and 1% for nonresidents who work in the city. Modeled on gross wages. The $52 local services tax owed to the workplace is not included. Act 32 collectors administer withholding; confirm the current rate sheet if your municipality differs from city+school.

jurisdictions.name: Detroit

source.name: City of Detroit income tax

jurisdictions.notes: Detroit's resident rate is 2.4%. Michigan law sets the nonresident city rate at half the resident rate, 1.2%, on income earned in the city. The estimate uses gross wages and does not apply the city's exemptions or the nonresident allocation form. Traditional 401(k) treatment can differ from federal; this model leaves deferrals in the Detroit base.

jurisdictions.name: Columbus, Ohio

source.name: City of Columbus income tax division

jurisdictions.notes: Columbus withholds 2.5% municipal income tax on qualifying wages earned in the city. Traditional 401(k) deferrals are generally excluded from Ohio municipal qualifying wages, and this model excludes them along with Section 125 amounts. If you live in one Ohio city and work in another, a credit usually prevents full double taxation. This estimate applies only the city you select.

jurisdictions.name: Cleveland

jurisdictions.notes: Cleveland's municipal income tax rate is 2.5%. Same qualifying-wage and one-city credit limits as the Columbus model.

jurisdictions.name: Montgomery County, Maryland

source.name: Comptroller of Maryland, Withholding Tax Facts 2026

jurisdictions.notes: Montgomery County's 2026 local income tax rate is 3.20% of Maryland taxable net income. Every Maryland county plus Baltimore City levies a local rate; many are named in this file. Counties not listed (or Anne Arundel/Frederick tiered schedules you want to override) can use the custom percent. The nonresident switch uses 2.25%, the rate Maryland uses for many nonresident withholding situations, and is a simplification.

jurisdictions.name: Baltimore City

source.name: Comptroller of Maryland, Withholding Tax Facts 2026

jurisdictions.notes: Baltimore City's 2026 local rate is 3.20% of Maryland taxable net income. Nonresident switch uses the 2.25% simplification described on the Montgomery County record.

jurisdictions.name: Marion County, Indiana

source.name: Indiana Department of Revenue, Departmental Notice #1 (county tax rates)

jurisdictions.notes: Marion County (Indianapolis) local income tax is 2.02% on the Indiana DOR Departmental Notice #1 county chart for 2026 (unchanged on the Oct. 1, 2026 revision). County of residence on January 1 controls for residents; nonresidents are taxed on the employment county. This estimate uses 2.02% for both switches. Additional major Indiana counties are also named; use the custom percent for counties not listed.

jurisdictions.name: Portland / Multnomah County
jurisdictions.residentOnlyNote: Metro and Multnomah income taxes apply to residents of those districts. Working in Portland while living in Vancouver, Washington, does not trigger them.

source.name: City of Portland Revenue Division, Personal Income Tax (Metro SHS + Multnomah PFA)

jurisdictions.notes: A Portland resident inside both Metro and Multnomah County is modeled with two taxes on Oregon taxable income: 1% Metro supportive housing services above the 2026 inflation-indexed thresholds of $128,000 single / $205,000 joint (was $125,000 / $200,000 for 2021–2025), plus Multnomah Preschool for All at 1.5% above $125,000 single / $200,000 joint and another 1.5% above $250,000 single / $400,000 joint. Sources: Portland.gov personal-tax page and Metro SHS revenue forecast. These taxes are filed with the Oregon return; not every employer withholds them. Someone in Washington County Metro but outside Multnomah would owe only the Metro layer — this combined jurisdiction is the Portland-in-Multnomah case.

Residents owe it on earnings wherever earned; nonresidents owe it on earnings within city limits. Modeled on gross wages. Voters renewed the tax in April 2026 for another five-year period. Retirement and similar non-earned income is outside this wage model.
